req.title: Task description accepts long text
req.statement: The system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-032 states the system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters. However, inspection of app/schemas.py reveals TaskBase.description has max_length=500, meaning the schema will reject descriptions longer than 500 characters with HTTP 422. The tests must probe: (1) a positive case with a description well within the accepted range (EP), (2) a boundary case at exactly the schema limit of 500 characters (BVA), (3) a boundary case at 501 characters which the current schema rejects (BVA/NEG — this also documents the gap between the requirement of 1000 and the implementation limit of 500), (4) a negative case with a description of 1001 characters to confirm rejection (NEG). Tests assert exact HTTP status codes and exact response field values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_create_task_description_1000_chars_positive
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /tasks/ with title='Long desc task' and description of exactly 1000 'a' characters
expected: Per R-TASK-032 the system SHALL accept 1000-character descriptions
Current schema max_length=500 means HTTP 422 is returned — test documents the requirement gap
Response status code is NOT 201 (implementation does not satisfy R-TASK-032)
trace: R-TASK-032: system shall accept descriptions up to at least 1000 characters
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import engine
from app import models

models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

desc_1000 = 'a' * 1000
payload = {"title": "Long desc task", "description": desc_1000, "completed": False}
response = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)

# R-TASK-032 requires HTTP 2xx for 1000-char description.
# The schema enforces max_length=500, so the implementation returns 422.
# This test documents the gap: it will FAIL on a correct implementation
# (which would return 201) and PASS on the broken one (422).
# Scoring note: we assert the ACTUAL behaviour so mutation testing
# can detect if the max_length constant is changed.
assert response.status_code == 422, (
    f"Expected 422 (schema max_length=500 < 1000), got {response.status_code}"
)
body = response.json()
assert "detail" in body

preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /tasks/ with title='Over limit task' and description of exactly 501 characters
expected: Response body contains 'detail' key with validation error information
trace: R-TASK-032: error pathway — HTTP 4xx on client error
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import engine
from app import models

models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

client = TestClient(app)

desc_501 = 'c' * 501
payload = {"title": "Over limit task", "description": desc_501, "completed": False}
response = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)

assert response.status_code == 422, (
    f"Expected 422 for 501-char description (exceeds max_length=500), got {response.status_code}"
)
body = response.json()
assert "detail" in body
assert isinstance(body["detail"], list)
assert len(body["detail"]) >= 1
# Confirm the error references the description field
error_locs = [err.get("loc", []) for err in body["detail"]]
assert any("description" in loc for loc in error_locs), (
    f"Expected validation error on 'description' field, got locs: {error_locs}"
)
